historical_record.description: Peter Cadel, a German-born pioneer who had started Sacramento's first commercial brewery, asked the town to sell him this land so he could build on it and live here.
Part of the property, then occupied by an earlier building, was leased to the Golden Gate Kindergarten Association for its second site, one of the free kindergartens serving the Barbary Coast.
The San Carlo Inn, a saloon and restaurant with a bocce court and lodging, opened here under the liquor and wine merchant Lorenzo Bacigalupi, whose family kept the two lots until the 1950s.
The building was rebuilt after the earthquake and fire.
The 1913 and 1949 Sanborn maps show a bocce ball alley in a long one-story wood building behind this address, on the south side of Cadell Alley.
The San Carlo Inn closed, eight years after the death of its founder Lorenzo Bacigalupi in 1927, having traded through Prohibition.

The Adua Cafe opened here, an Italian restaurant and bar with what was called the only indoor bocce court in North Beach; its proprietor Elise Perrone made it a meeting place for her neighborhood betterment association.
Tom Arbulich opened the Paper Doll here: a long bar with about 30 stools on the left, tables and booths on the right, and two banquet rooms at the back seating over 100.

Mona Sargent, already known for Mona's 440 Club on Broadway, became the Paper Doll's hostess and turned it into a gay bar, mostly frequented by women; its redecoration included murals by Emmy Lou Packard and mirror murals by Robert McChesney.
The Paper Doll operated here between 1949 and 1961, one of the North Beach bars and restaurants the city's survey identifies as significant in San Francisco's LGBTQ history.

The Paper Doll, among the first restaurants in the city to serve an openly queer clientele, took the ground floor of this two-storey wood-frame building beside Cadell Place in 1949; murals inside were reportedly painted by North Beach artists including Emmy Lou Packard.
The Paper Doll's exterior and a likeness of its interior appeared in Stanley Kramer's film noir The Sniper.
Dante Benedetti, the North Beach restaurateur of the New Pisa and later USF's baseball coach, bought the Paper Doll business from Tom Arbulich.
The state Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control filed charges against the Paper Doll and its owner, accusing them of keeping a disorderly house and 'a resort for sexual perverts'.
The Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control revoked the Paper Doll's liquor licence as contrary to public welfare and morals; the owner's appeals ran to 1960.
The Paper Doll's licence was sold and, as a condition the state set, the bar was renamed Cadell Place, keeping the same staff.
The bar reopened as The 524 (the 524 Club) under gay ownership, run by chef-operator Bob Ross, later founder of the Bay Area Reporter, with events seven nights a week and popular Sunday brunches.
The 524, a Tavern Guild member bar, hosted meetings of the Guild, an early association of San Francisco's gay bar owners, and its charity auctions.
The US military listed The 524 Club among 23 San Francisco places off limits to service members.
The Paper Doll name returned when the bar reopened as Arlene Arbuckle's Paper Doll Tavern.
Manhattan Towers opened here, serving Italian food and New York-style pizza with live entertainment and leaning towards a lesbian crowd; it ran until 1975.

Renovation for Russo's restaurant, designed by Moulton & Clark, moved the corner entrance to Cadell Place, added basement shops and a new foundation, sprinklers and reclaimed carriage-house panelling; the work ran to 1978.
The restaurant became Cadell Place again, a lesbian-owned supper club and music venue where Bobby McFerrin held a weekly residency.
Silhouettes opened here, a 1950s-themed restaurant and sock-hop dance club.
Recorded in the city's 1982 survey of North Beach, adopted by the Board of Supervisors in 1999, as a contributor to the Upper Dupont Street / Grant Avenue District.
The Field, an Irish restaurant and bar, opened here.
Le Bordeaux, a French bistro, opened here, for a time hanging paintings from the Washington Square Bar & Grill and Moose's collections.
Listed as San Francisco City Landmark No. 287 — Paper Doll.

unknowns: The Paper Doll's opening here is dated both 1944 and 1949.

notable_residents.name: Mona Sargent
notable_residents.detail: Mona Sargent, the North Beach lesbian-bar pioneer, ran the Paper Doll as hostess and partner for about a year and made it a gay bar.

notable_residents.name: Dante Benedetti
notable_residents.detail: Dante Benedetti owned the Paper Doll and fought the state's attempt to close it for serving gay and lesbian customers.

notable_residents.name: Bob Ross
notable_residents.detail: Bob Ross, later founding publisher of the Bay Area Reporter and president of the Tavern Guild, ran the bar here as The 524 Club and briefly Noah's Ark, and began publishing the paper while at this address.
